sources.title: U.S. War Department, TM-E30-480,1October1944, ChapterIX, SectionIV
sources.kind: Primary wartime intelligence manual, modern transcription
supports: The Model89A description states a360-degree turret traverse.
The section's general armament description identifies ball-mounted machine guns on Japanese light/medium tanks, including hull and rear-turret positions.
The Type89 running gear description identifies rear-sprocket drive.
sources.limits: The manual contains wartime identification and measurement uncertainties. Its variant names and approximate dimensions are not used as factory drawings or proof of this museum vehicle's exact machine-gun stops.

sources.title: U.S. Military Intelligence Service, Japanese Tanks and Tank Tactics, Special Series26,15November1944, Medium Tanks
sources.kind: Primary wartime intelligence publication, modern transcription
supports: The89A entry identifies a turret capable of360-degree traverse, a hull machine gun and a rear-turret machine gun.
The publication describes rear-sprocket drive and the Diesel89B development.
sources.limits: Model94 terminology and inconsistent gun data in later entries are not imported into the selected Otsu reconstruction.

displayBehavior.tracks: Left/right distance clocks independently move the real track-link nodes; all30 wheel groups rotate by their effective radius.
displayBehavior.turret: Continuous full-circle rotation about its vertical pivot; main gun pitch/recoil remain independent.
displayBehavior.machineGuns: Two independent finite yaw/pitch controls within each mounting frame. The rear mounting flange remains fixed while its gun carrier moves.
displayBehavior.rangeClassification: Model display/clearance limits; exact factory firing arcs and traverse rates remain unverified.
displayBehavior.bowDoorGunStow: Opening the door blends the hull gun to+10deg yaw/+8deg pitch before the swept door reaches the jacket; inferred display linkage, not a sourced original procedure

historicalBoundary: This validates plausible articulated display of the reconstructed museum appearance. It does not establish this vehicle or type participating in the16-18March1938 Tengxian city assault.
